subject: Tenant billing slice: playbook + UX constraints for console tile
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant billing slice: playbook + UX constraints for console tile

Folks —

Thanks for carving out time this week. I want to consolidate asks coming from both Sales (BrightOps) and Platform teams into a short playbook we can hand to Console for an initial ship. High-level request: a console tile that surfaces per-tenant billing slices (token costs broken down by route/model variant), sample tail-latency percentiles, and an exportable line-item CSV that matches billing attribution.

Key constraints to consider up front (derived from BrightOps call, attached mockup_v1):
- Data latency target: tile should show data window no older than 30 minutes for live troubleshooting; historical queries can be hourly.
- Sampling: we should avoid full-stream aggregation for cost — propose probabilistic sampling with deterministic weighting so exports match chargebacks.
- Drilldown: tile must allow drill-to-route and drill-to-session (kv-cache hits vs cold tokens).
- RBAC: tenant-level data only shown to support/admin roles; billing users should see aggregate but not PII-associated traces.

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus — technical feasibility and rough estimation (SLO impact, query cost)
2) Jasmine — UX constraints and recommended drill pattern (one-click vs modal)
3) Karthik — product/roadmap alignment (does this slot into Observability Q3 work or separate)

I've attached a quick PNG mock and a short notes file. BrightOps is willing to be a design partner for initial feedback (Emily copied in this thread). Can we get rough answers in 48 hours?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant billing slice: playbook + UX constraints for console tile

Thanks Irene — good concise set. Quick follow-ups from infra/telemetry perspective:

1) Sampling and export alignment:
- We can support probabilistic sampling if we persist sample weights and the exact sampled token counts per request. That requires augmenting our ingest records with a sample_weight field so offline aggregation can rehydrate to full counts; storage delta ~8-12% depending on schema.
- If the CSV must match invoice-level tokenization (tokenization used for billing), we need an offline join to the billing-enriched events which currently are batched hourly. That will add up to 60–90s extra export latency for an "export now" flow.

2) Live data window: 30-minute freshness for the dashboard is achievable if we limit queries to pre-aggregated hourly + recent delta shards. Fully raw-live queries at tenant scale will blow query costs. Recommend hybrid approach: pre-aggregates per 5–15 minute windows + incremental delta for the last 30 minutes.

3) SLO impact: the aggregation pipelines will add 5–8% more write throughput during peak ingest; no significant read-side latency impact if we index by tenant and route. We should plan for a canary with 5–10 high-volume tenants first.

Estimate: small spike work with one backend engineer + one infra engineer + two analysts for a 4-week MVP (includes exports and RBAC gating). If we remove export fidelity to invoice tokens, MVP reduces to ~2 weeks.

I'll flag a doc with schema changes and cost delta later today.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Infra
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant billing slice: playbook + UX constraints for console tile

Great thread. From a UX standpoint — a few non-negotiables and recommendations so Console PM/Design have clear guardrails:

Non-negotiables:
- Single-click CSV export that includes the same aggregation keys users see in the UI (tenant_id, route, model_variant, timestamp window, token_count, unit_cost). If we can't guarantee exact invoice token mapping, surface a "reconciles to invoice" badge only when reconciliation has completed.
- Drill behavior: default tile shows top 5 routes by cost; clicking a route opens a right-rail with time-series and a sample set of request traces (scrubbed). The right-rail should show cache hit/miss toggle so support can quickly triage cold models.
- Permission model: billing role sees tenant-level totals and exports; support role sees drilldowns but with trace redaction. Admins can enable debugging traces.

Performance/UX tradeoffs:
- If Marcus goes with pre-aggregates + deltas, we'll show a "last updated" timestamp and an explicit "refresh" CTA to re-run the delta join. That keeps expectations clear.
- For canary tenants, we should add a small banner in the tile: "Canary data — full fidelity exports for selected tenants only."

I've attached a revised mockup (mockup_v2.pdf) with proposed right-rail flow and an export modal. Also added micro-copy for the reconciliation states. Happy to take this to Console design sync and present the flows.

Jasmine Liu
Staff Product Designer, Console
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mockup_v2.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Emily Suarez <emily@brightops.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jul 2028 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant billing slice: playbook + UX constraints for console tile

Hi team — thanks for pulling this together and for the thoughtful constraints. Quick note from BrightOps:

- The export fidelity is our blocker for adoption — our finance team needs line items that reconcile to invoice for internal showbacks. If you need a pilot tenant for the canary, we're happy to volunteer one of our production tenants.
- On sampling: deterministic weights are critical because we run automated chargeback scripts. If you can provide the weight field in the CSV, we can reconstruct charges locally while you iterate.
- The right-rail flow looks great — one ask: can the sample traces include the top 3 prompt prefixes (redacted) so we can triage cost spikes faster?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute session next week to demo our finance use case and provide sample exports.

—Emily
Emily Suarez
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightOps
